biodiversity_overview.text: 216,030 GBIF occurrence records for 101 tracked species are attributed to Karnataka, spanning 1777-2026.
197,726 of these records (91.5%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 29, Magnoliopsida 21, Mammalia 19, Squamata 10, Amphibia 7, Actinopterygii 7, Testudines 4, Crocodylia 1, Cephalopoda 1, Liliopsida 1, Elasmobranchii 1.

threatened_species.text: 11 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Asian Elephant (EN), Mugger Crocodile (VU), Tiger (EN), Sloth Bear (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Spot-billed Duck (17,275), Indian Paradise-flycatcher (16,359), Indian White-eye (15,164), Common Peafowl (15,026), Indian Golden Oriole (14,654).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 10,055 in 2016 to 1,252 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 4.76% of Karnataka's area (54 areas intersect the state).
11.2% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (22,242 of 197,726); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), Indian Courser (0.47), Mugger Crocodile (0.46), Indian Glaskilli (0.46).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Karnataka (equal-weight reference): cell near 13.125N 74.625E (overall rank 8, median rank across weightings 16); cell near 13.125N 77.625E (overall rank 25, median rank across weightings 39); cell near 12.375N 76.875E (overall rank 62, median rank across weightings 80).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 22,850 km2 (12.01% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

579.0 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (2.53% of the 2000 extent; 1.34% in 2015-2024, rank 12 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2023 (51.02 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 1.15% of land and population density is 371.3 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
21% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
